body:
Make design runs faster and less error-prone, based on the design agent's own report after it drew the Board page layout. That report said understanding the page was easy. The hard part was working out the design format and writing a big hand-built proposal with no way to check it first.

## Asked for

- Fix the design agent's issues (human, from the agent's report).

## In this feature

- **The format, from one command.** The agent can list every element type with its required and optional properties, the values each one allows, and a minimal example. Today it has to read source code and test data to learn this.
- **Check before proposing.** The agent can check a set of changes against the design's rules and see a short outline of the result, without asking the human. Today the only check is a real proposal, so a single mistake means another proposal and another wait.
- **Add a whole branch at once.** One add can carry an element with its children nested inside it, and Solace gives out ids that aren't already taken. Today every element is a separate add with an id the agent writes by hand.

## Suggested (cursory, not prescriptive)

- The format list comes from the same table the design rules use (`design.ELEMENT_TYPES`), so it can't fall out of step with them.
- The check uses the same steps as `design propose` (D-241 point 3: apply to a copy, then `design.validate`), but leaves out the question to the human. Whether it's a separate command or a flag on propose is up to the work. Spec 15 lists the design run's commands and needs updating either way.

## Open

- New element types (menu/tabs with a current item, scroll area, split pane, badge, notice, card accent, a stand-in for an embedded component, one screen that changes with window size). Each one changes what designs can show, so they wait for the human to choose.

## Not in this feature

- A command that shows how a page's code is laid out ("page anatomy"). That's general code reading, not design work.
- A shared Shell menu design. The design agent can make it in a normal design run. It doesn't need new tooling.
title: design: agent tooling
